author: WP18
summary: Updated-for-d6e9ff05 chapter on running cross-built Windows tests under Wine: isolated prefixes, which translation runtime serves each renderer, log-marker engagement gates, Direct2D's environment controls, the D3D12 Proton route, the Direct3D 9 oracle and the limits of translated execution. Current at TARGET. The Direct3D gates, Proton root cause and oracle findings were already on the renderer deep dives; the Direct2D and GDI residue, Proton pinning asymmetry, prefix hygiene and tiers are on the new Windows deep dive.

figures.note: Redrawn with the current runtimes only (DXVK, vkd3d-proton, Wine built-in d2d1/gdi32); runtime nodes that served retired renderer families were dropped.

concepts.section: Windows II: Wine and Engagement Gates
concepts.text: Cross-compilation proves only that a Windows-shaped program exists; exit status cannot tell whether the intended DirectX implementation ran, because Wine can fall back to its own WineD3D stack and still draw a plausible image.

concepts.section: Prefixes isolate incompatible runtime stacks
concepts.text: Named prefixes isolate runtime stacks: ~/.wine for the Direct2D Wine path (or CNA_DIRECT2D_WINEPREFIX), ~/.wine-cna-d3d11 shared by the D3D9 and D3D11 DXVK lanes, and ~/.wine-cna-d3d12 for vkd3d-proton.

concepts.section: Prefixes isolate incompatible runtime stacks
concepts.text: The Direct2D fresh-prefix suite runs the whole Direct2D label in a throwaway prefix whose only dependency is wineboot --init (no winetricks, overrides or DXVK), so a pass cannot depend on accumulated prefix state.

concepts.section: Prefixes isolate incompatible runtime stacks
concepts.text: Special-purpose prefixes hold Microsoft's d3dcompiler_47.dll and a real 32-bit XNA 4.0 installation for the oracle; isolation of bitness, overrides and runtimes is the contract and prefix count is not an architecture metric.

concepts.section: Prefixes isolate incompatible runtime stacks
concepts.text: A prefix is mutable system state; both Proton launchers hard-refuse ~/.wine after a Proton wine run without WINEPREFIX silently upgraded a personal prefix and hung in a Mono wizard, and the Proton prefix bootstrap is bounded by timeout --kill-after.

concepts.section: Which translation runtime owns each renderer
concepts.text: Runtime per renderer on the Linux loop: DIRECTX9 via DXVK d3d9, DIRECTX11 via DXVK d3d11+dxgi, DIRECTX12 via vkd3d-proton d3d12/d3d12core, DIRECT2D via Wine's built-in d2d1/d3d11/dxgi or a pinned Proton, GDI via Wine's gdi32 with no wrapper.

concepts.section: Which translation runtime owns each renderer
concepts.text: The same test executable can traverse Wine built-in code, DXVK or vkd3d-proton depending on its prefix, so a generic 'ran under Wine' label hides the implementation under test.

concepts.section: An engagement gate turns logs into a verdict
concepts.text: The D3D9/11 launchers require a 'DXVK:' log line and the D3D12 launcher 'vkd3d-proton - applicationVersion:'; a missing marker ends the run with exit status 3 naming the likely silent fallback.

concepts.section: An engagement gate turns logs into a verdict
concepts.text: Device-free discovery cannot emit a marker, so it uses a narrowly named bypass (CNA_D3D11_SKIP_DXVK_GATE=1 and siblings) that normal smoke and pixel runs must not set.

concepts.section: An engagement gate turns logs into a verdict
concepts.text: An allow-WineD3D switch changes the oracle rather than producing an equivalent pass; the transferable gate design is a positive implementation-specific marker, capture of the whole run, and failure when it is absent.
tokens: fail when the marker is absent

concepts.section: An engagement gate turns logs into a verdict
concepts.text: Direct2D has no d2d1 engagement marker and every Direct2D registration bypasses the inherited DXVK gate, so a mis-provisioned prefix could yield a result without proving which Direct2D path ran; GDI has no wrapper at all.

concepts.section: Environment-specific workarounds are part of the evidence
concepts.text: Direct2D's isolated-Xvfb runner (private X authority, known geometry) and fresh-prefix suite describe the environment in which a result holds; they must not be generalised into renderer behaviour on genuine Windows.
tokens: not renderer behaviour on genuine Windows

concepts.section: Environment-specific workarounds are part of the evidence
concepts.text: Hardware-backed DXVK/vkd3d results name their adapter (a recorded AMD Radeon 780M with Mesa RADV) so that a Vulkan software implementation such as llvmpipe is never mistaken for GPU evidence.

concepts.section: D3D12 and Proton require matched ownership
concepts.text: Plain Wine's dxgi and a separately overridden vkd3d-proton d3d12 do not share the command-queue ABI needed for swap chains, so the swap-chain lane runs end-to-end through Proton, where CreateSwapChainForHwnd succeeded (CNA's record).

concepts.section: D3D12 and Proton require matched ownership
concepts.text: The Proton launchers do not share version discipline: Direct2D reads a pin file (Proton 9.0 (Beta), then Proton 8.0) and refuses Experimental unless CNA_DIRECT2D_PROTON_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL=1, while the D3D12 launcher defaults to 'Proton - Experimental' (overridable with CNA_D3D12_PROTON_DIR).
concepts.note: The D3D12 asymmetry is also recorded as WP19-i002.

concepts.section: D3D12 and Proton require matched ownership
concepts.text: The Direct2D Proton result was produced with a fabricated Steam tree and left no surviving prefix, whereas the D3D12 Proton prefix remained on the development machine.

concepts.section: The D3D9 oracle controls both sides
concepts.text: Microsoft's stock-effect .fx sources compiled with genuine d3dcompiler_47.dll under Wine match FNA's shipped bytecode in 61 of 66 variants (the rest narrowed to compiler version), and Wine's built-in compiler is not an adequate substitute.

target.evidence: CNA shader-parity records (see the DIRECTX9 fidelity page)

concepts.section: The D3D9 oracle controls both sides
concepts.text: The pixel oracle renders one declarative scene through real XNA 4.0 in a 32-bit prefix and through CNA's MinGW DIRECTX9 renderer, both over the same engaged DXVK path, with a mutation-tested comparator proving that changed pixels are detected.

target.evidence: oracle tooling and D3D9_XNA_Diff registration (see those pages)

concepts.section: The D3D9 oracle controls both sides
concepts.text: A8B8G8R8 is legal for D3D9 textures but not for a primary back buffer; CNA substitutes A8R8G8B8 only at back-buffer creation and readback handles both byte orders.

concepts.section: What translated execution cannot prove
concepts.text: DXVK synthesises D3DCAPS9 from a modern Vulkan device, so CNA's capability interpretation and XNA-matching output through DXVK are not observations of a period Windows driver; D3D11 and D3D12 still run through translation.

concepts.section: What translated execution cannot prove
concepts.text: The remaining high-value check needs a person on Windows hardware (device loss, fullscreen, real XNA outside Wine); until then the precise claim is 'pixel-verified against XNA through the same engaged DXVK path on the recorded GPU'.
tokens: pixel-verified against XNA through the same engaged DXVK path

issues.text: The Direct2D Wine lane has no d2d1 engagement marker and every Direct2D registration bypasses the DXVK gate, so which Direct2D implementation ran is shown only by environment controls.
